title: Add adaptive degeneration detector and circuit-breaker for gradual tail regressions
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Added an adaptive degeneration detector that monitors tail entropy and traffic sparsity to trigger a canary circuit-breaker. New detector reduces noisy false positives and provides automatic rollback/fallback to baseline model when sustained tail regressions are detected.
description: Summary: Implements an adaptive degeneration detector plus an automated circuit-breaker that pauses or narrows canary traffic when gradual tail latency regressions or entropy-driven degeneration appear. Motivation: Existing canary detectors are sensitive to bursty noise and fail to discriminate sparse but meaningful tail degradations that impact end-user SLAs over long horizons. This change introduces a rate-aware, entropy-weighted signal and a hold/fallback circuit that integrates into the canary control plane. Key changes: (1) degeneration_detector.py implements an entropy-weighted tail score combining percentile deltas, sample sparsity weight, and a decaying confidence window; (2) circuit_breaker.go implements the state machine (OPEN->HALF_OPEN->CLOSED) plus progressive traffic throttling and automatic baseline fallback variant selection; (3) perf-harness replay recipe and synthetic benchmark to calibrate thresholds; (4) dashboards and alerting rules for ownership visibility; (5) unit and integration tests exercising borderline and gradual scenarios. Commit summary: commit 1: implement entropy-weighted tail scoring and window manager (degeneration_detector.py). commit 2: add circuit-breaker orchestration and SDK hooks (circuit_breaker.go, canary/README.md). commit 3: add perf-harness replay recipe and synthetic benchmarks. commit 4: tests, docs, dashboards and CI pipeline updates. Files changed (high-level): detectors, orchestrator, perf harness, dashboards, docs, metrics library, CI config, Helm values. Tests: added targeted unit tests that simulate slowly-increasing 95/99th latency bands and sparsity-conditioned noise; added an end-to-end canary test that validates the circuit transitions and fallback to baseline. Local perf results: in offline replay with production trace A the new detector flagged a sustained 99th percentile uplift of ~22% over 18 hours with an entropy score above threshold while throughput remained flat; when the circuit-breaker engaged traffic to baseline the observed product 99p returned to baseline within 15 minutes in replay. Perf-harness smoke in CI initially failed due to flaky synthetic seed; reran with fixed seed and all perf checks passed. Review conversation: Diego: "Nice approach. Two asks: add comment explaining the decay constant choice and expose it as a config in Helm." Author reply: "Added config and inline comment; moved decay constant to chart values and documented rationale in docs/perf/degeneration_detector.md." Liam: "Please add a small e2e to cover HALF_OPEN->CLOSED path under injected small bursts." Author reply: "Added e2e scenario in canary/tests/test_degen_detector.py that drives the state machine and asserts safe rollback." Priya: "Can we surface the main scoring metric in Console so SREs can correlate with traces?" Author reply: "Dashboards updated and we emit tail_entropy_metric with tags for model and canary_id; included JSONNET panel in dashboards/perf/degeneration_alerts.jsonnet." Code review: two rounds of comments addressed, one thread on locking in the Go state machine required moving to a mutex-protected microstate which was implemented. CI: build -> pass, unit tests -> pass, perf-pipeline -> rerun -> pass. Risk and mitigations: False positives were a primary concern. Mitigations include adaptive thresholding tied to traffic sparsity, cooldown hysteresis, staged HALF_OPEN probing and an explicit human review threshold before full automated rollback (configurable). Backwards compatibility: no breaking API changes. The new detector is off by default for existing canary profiles and must be opt-in via canary config. Rollout plan: enable canary in staging for two weeks, collect telemetry, then opt-in for 10% of production traffic for another week before full enable. Related work: follows on ENG-3287 (tail stability effort) and complements canary-stability guards from ENG-3310. Merge: squashed and merged into main 2026-03-02 after approvals by Diego and Liam. Notes for on-call: runbooks updated in docs/perf/degeneration_detector.md and linked in the Console alert. Additional follow-ups: tune decay constant per region, surface per-model baseline selector in Console, add a lightweight approximate-KL variant to compare distributions when sampling budgets allow.
